sweeperExclusions.quote: This request shall not be construed as authorization to proceed with or be paid for charges incurred by performing any of the work called for in this solicitation.
In providing these instructions, the Government's intention is to solicit information that will permit a competitive evaluation of the Offeror's proposal.
The information solicited will demonstrate the Offeror's competence and understanding of requirements and the capability to successfully complete all the requirements specified in the Medevac SOW.

Telephone questions will not be accepted.
Travelers will not be required to be pre-enrolled or registered in a Contractor's system in order for the Contractor to provide services covered under this contract.
NASA will not provide arbitration or remediation to resolve disputes between the Contractor and traveler regarding reimbursements of uncovered expenses.
*NASA will recognize other equivalent regulatory agencies when carriers are not governed by the aforementioned federal aviation regulations.
The Government does not assume liability that results from claims that arise from their direct performance of this contract.

rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure its owned, leased, or chartered aircraft comply with applicable aircraft and pilot requirements, including for subcontractors.

rows.verbatim:
Aircraft used for NASA traveler transportation shall be certificated, operated, and maintained in accordance with the requirements of 14 CFR:
a. Part 21—Certification Procedures for Products and Parts
b. Part 25—Airworthiness Standards: Transport Category Airplanes Part 29—Airworthiness Standards:
Transport Category Rotorcraft Part 39—Airworthiness Directives
c. Part 43—Maintenance, Preventative Maintenance, Rebuilding, and Alteration Part 61—Certification: Pilots,
Flight Instructors, and Ground Instructors
d. Part 65—Certification: Airmen Other Than Flight Crewmembers Part 91—General Operating and Flight Rules
e. Part 135—Operating Requirements: Commuter and On-Demand Operations
rows.normalized: Aircraft used for NASA traveler transportation shall be certificated, operated, and maintained per 14 CFR Parts 21, 25, 29, 39, 43, 61, 65, 91, and 135.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall have a documented Safety Management System (SMS) in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), Federal, and industry standards.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall have a documented Safety Management System per ICAO, Federal, and industry standards.

rows.verbatim:
Requirements include the following:
a. A structured means of safety risk management decision making.
b. A means of demonstrating safety management capability before system failures occur.
c. Increased confidence in risk controls through structured safety assurance processes.
d. An effective interface for knowledge sharing.
e. A safety promotion framework to support a sound safety culture.
rows.normalized: SMS requirements include: structured safety risk decision-making, demonstrating safety capability before failures, risk-control confidence via safety assurance, effective knowledge-sharing interface, and a safety promotion framework; 5 items total.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall indemnify the Government for any occurrence, action, or claim that might trigger the Government's liability; unless the Government is found to be liable.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall indemnify the Government for claims triggering Government liability, unless the Government is found liable.

rows.verbatim: The rights and obligations of the parties under this clause shall survive the termination, expiration, or completion of this contract.
rows.normalized: The parties' rights and obligations under this clause shall survive termination, expiration, or completion of the contract.

Contractor shall provide medical travel services worldwide on a pre-paid basis, including 14 specified services (a-n): transportation, provider coordination, pharmacy assistance, medical monitoring, medication/vaccine/blood/device assistance, referrals, patient advocacy, bedside case management, translation services, hospital admittance/discharge coordination, hospital payment coordination, insurance coordination, GOP/pay-as-agent services, and repatriation of remains.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall transport the injured or ill traveler to nearest appropriate medical facility that practices U.S. standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall transport injured/ill travelers to the nearest medical facility practicing U.S. standards of care.

rows.verbatim: In the event that the medical facility does not meet the U.S. standards of medical care, the Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and NASA Contracting Officer Representative (COR) for using the proposed facility.
rows.normalized: If the proposed medical facility does not meet U.S. standards of care, Contractor shall provide rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for timely communication, integration and operational protocols with NASA physicians, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for communication, integration, protocols with NASA physicians, and medical report dissemination.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall obtain all necessary insurance information from the traveler, as required, and shall coordinate the payment of personal medical expenses incurred by the traveler that are not arranged for or provided directly by the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain required insurance information from the traveler and coordinate payment of personal medical expenses not arranged by the Contractor.

rows.verbatim: Such coordination shall be conducted exclusively between the Contractor, the traveler, and the traveler’s insurer, without any involvement from the Government.
rows.normalized: Such coordination shall occur only between the Contractor, the traveler, and the traveler's insurer, without Government involvement.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B FFP Group Membership.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide an “Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation” (medevac) service in response to a worldwide medical emergency for NASA’s Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD), Johnson Space Center (JSC), or other travelers identified by NASA (referred to as ‘traveler(s)’ throughout) on a pre-paid basis regardless of traveler’s home location or country of origin.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation service worldwide on a pre-paid basis for NASA-identified travelers.

rows.verbatim: b. The Contractor shall provide transportation for three accompanying travelers specified by NASA on the same transport as the injured/ill individual requiring a medevac.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transportation for three accompanying travelers specified by NASA on the same medevac transport.

rows.verbatim: c. In the event that the same transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, at least one accompanying traveler specified by NASA shall be accommodated on the same transport.
rows.normalized: If the transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, Contractor must accommodate at least one on the same transport.

rows.verbatim: d. The Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA Contracting Officer Representative (COR) why it cannot transport all accompanying travelers and provide alternate transportation for the remaining accompanying travelers within 24 hours to the same location as the injured or ill traveler.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide rationale to the COR for inability to transport all accompanying travelers and provide alternate transportation for remaining travelers within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim: 2.2.2. The Contractor provided services shall meet the Commission on Accreditation Medical Transport Services (CAMTS), National Accreditation Alliance of Medical Transport Applications (NAAMTA) Global, and European Aero-Medical Institute (EURAMI) accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.
rows.normalized: Contractor's services must meet CAMTS, NAAMTA Global, or EURAMI accreditation standards (or equivalent) for personnel and assets.

rows.verbatim: Active credentials must be maintained according to the standard renewal timelines dictated by the respective accrediting body.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain active accreditation credentials per the accrediting body's renewal timelines.

rows.verbatim: Any deviations must be reported to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and Contracting Officer Representative (COR), and approved by NASA prior to implementation, unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report any deviations from accreditation standards to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR and obtain NASA approval before implementation.

The decision to perform a medevac shall be made jointly (50/50) by NASA and the
Contractor, who will apply U.S. standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: NASA and Contractor jointly (50/50) decide whether to perform a medevac, applying U.S. standards of medical care.

rows.verbatim: This independent third party will be mutually agreed upon within 30 calendar days of contract award.
rows.normalized: NASA and Contractor must mutually agree on an independent third party within 30 calendar days of contract award.

2.3.1. The Contractor shall conduct a program status meeting each contract year with NASA management and JSC's
Chief Medical Officer, with the first meeting happening within 90 calendar days of the start of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct an annual program status meeting with NASA management and JSC's Chief Medical Officer, first meeting within 90 calendar days of contract start.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.3. The Contractor shall provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and update annually for currency by Oct
1st, a Medical Facility Support Plan for each of the Russia and Kazakhstan medical facilities identified by NASA
which contains the following:
a. Points of Contact (primary, alternate, and emergency) and communication protocols, including
language/translation support and expected response times.
b. Medical Capabilities and Transport Capabilities, including bed‑to‑bed transport feasibility, equipment
availability, access to specialized care, and any seasonal or regional constraints that may affect operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide (within 60 days, updated annually by Oct 1) a Medical Facility Support Plan for Russia/Kazakhstan facilities containing at least items a-h (continues on next page); this row covers items a-b.

rows.verbatim:
c. Admittance, Use, GOP, and Discharge Processes, including procedures required to initiate care, provide
ongoing coordination, and transfer patients between facilities and medevac resources.
d. Insurance Acceptance Status, identifying whether each facility accepts U.S. Government employee medical
insurance plans and any known payment requirements, pre‑payment expectations, or dispute‑resolution
considerations.
e. Facility Use Recommendations, including NASA‑specific considerations and any operational limitations or
risk factors.
f. Regional Risk Assessment, summarizing relevant geopolitical, infrastructure, transportation, or environmental
risks, along with proposed mitigation strategies.
g. Transport and Access Considerations, including typical timelines and constraints for access to airports, border
crossings, restricted areas, or local authorities.
h. Verification and Validation Procedures, describing how the Contractor annually confirms the accuracy of
facility information, capabilities, and points of contact data.
rows.normalized: Continuation of Medical Facility Support Plan required contents (items c-h) from SOW 2.3.3, carried over from page 7.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.4. The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and maintain for the duration
of the contract, the GOP advance service agreements with the specific medical facilities that NASA identifies as
critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish, provide (within 60 days), and maintain GOP advance service agreements with NASA-identified critical medical facilities in Russia/Kazakhstan.

rows.verbatim:
If the Contractor cannot establish a GOP advance service agreement at one of NASA's identified medical facilities in
Russia/Kazakhstan by the end of that 60-day period, then the Contractor shall notify the NASA COR and provide an
alternate course of action to meet the intent of the GOP advance service agreement.
rows.normalized: If Contractor cannot establish a GOP agreement within 60 days, it must notify the COR and propose an alternate course of action.

rows.verbatim:
Annually by December 15th, the Contractor shall provide a written summary report on the status of GOP advance
service agreements for the NASA identified hospitals.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a written GOP agreement status report annually by December 15th.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.5. The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and updated annually for
currency by Oct 1st, a written medevac plan of action/response for each location that NASA frequently visits to
include Moscow, Russia; Baikonur, Kazakhstan; Karaganda, Kazakhstan; Nordwijk, Netherlands; Montreal,
Canada; Tsukuba, Japan; and Tanegashima, Japan. The plan shall include at a minimum:
a. Specific points of contact the Contractor will utilize to access restricted airports or facilities;
b. Unique country and local specific requirements for medevac services and plans on how to address each;
c. Specific facilities, capabilities, and transport services in country the Contractor will utilize for bed-to-bed
medical transport including any operational limitations or risk factors;
d. Transport and Access Considerations, including typical timelines and constraints for access to airports, border
crossings, restricted areas, or local authorities.
e. Regional Risk Assessment, summarizing relevant geopolitical, infrastructure, transportation, or environmental
risks, along with proposed mitigation strategies.
f. Whether selected medical providers accept U.S Government employee medical insurance plans;
g. List of data and documentation the Contractor requires NASA to provide to support medevac.
h. Verification and Validation Procedures, describing how the Contractor annually confirms the accuracy of
facility information, capabilities, and points of contact data.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide (within 60 days, updated annually by Oct 1) a written medevac plan of action for listed locations, containing at minimum items a-h.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.6. The Contractor shall provide, within 10 calendar days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability
that:
a. Provides travelers with a description of the scope of Contractor's services in accordance with this SOW.
b. Educates travelers on specific instructions to follow should a medical incident or emergency occur and
traveler's responsibilities in accordance with this SOW.
c. Captures critical information from travelers that expedites medical assistance and evacuation when
necessary.
d. Meets industry standards for data protection, accessibility, storage, and retention requirements of private
medical and personal information (e.g. Personally Identifiable Information, Health Insurance, etc.).
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, within 10 days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability meeting requirements a-d.

Within 36 hours of NASA reservation, the Contractor shall provide a Reservation Readiness Package consisting of a
dedicated tail-number assignment, overflight and landing permits, diplomatic route clearances, aircraft medical and
transport capabilities, and staffing plan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a Reservation Readiness Package within 36 hours of NASA's reservation.

rows.verbatim:
NASA will provide call-up/execute notification to the Contractor no later than 36 hours prior to the Soyuz landing
event.
rows.normalized: Contractor can expect call-up/execute notification from NASA no later than 36 hours before the Soyuz landing event.

rows.verbatim: The crew member and the associated NASA flight surgeon shall be transported to Houston, Texas.

rows.verbatim:
Within 3 hours of the NASA call-up, the Contractor shall activate the asset and personnel and provide an Operational
Deployment Package consisting of a copy of the officially filed International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)
flight plan, crew-rest compliance, real-time satellite tracking link, confirmation of NASA passengers on flight
manifest, finalized staffing plan, and communications matrix.
rows.normalized: Contractor must activate asset/personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package within 3 hours of NASA's call-up.

rows.verbatim:

transport via air ambulance shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid
reservation fee and call-up fee as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will be
incurred by NASA or its travelers.
